notes:
Read from eleven recorded pages of the 2025 general-practice list (tests/fixtures/catalogue_pipeline/united_italian/): every page carrying a golden-sheet row, plus one of each layout. 282 rows, all conforming, no blocking issue (tests/test_united_italian_contract.py). The full document is 40 pages and 657 priced lines across 26 categories and 43 distributed brands.

Corroborated against the BizOps golden sheet: all thirteen of its coded rows were found on the recorded pages and eleven agree on price to the cent.

STILL OPEN at the time this was marked SUPPORTED, recorded here because clearing technical_debt is what SUPPORTED requires and these must not vanish with it:
  * 89471 — A 50x DISAGREEMENT, and the one to settle first. The sheet records the basis as CASE, so $52.00 buys fifty drapes. The page prints '(50's / case) $52.00 / pc' — fifty to a case and the price is PER PIECE. The contract reads the page. Pinned by test_the_sheet_and_the_page_disagree_about_89471_and_the_page_wins.
  * 3549232 Propofol — sheet $135.00, this list $320.00, same product. The sheet predates the 2025 list or is wrong; a person has to say which.
  * AHB1323HK appears TWICE on the sheet, as 'LRS Fluid Bag 500ml' and as '0.9% Nacl Fluid Bag 500ml'. The page says AHB1323HK is NaCl 0.9% 500ml and that Lactated Ringer 500ml is 2B2323Q, so one of those two sheet rows carries the wrong code.
  * The '/100's' rows resolve to PACK where the sheet records BOX. A DELIBERATE divergence on the 2026-09-01 ruling — the page states a quantity and names no vessel — pinned by test_the_sheet_names_a_container_the_page_never_prints.
  * SLEEVE is not a unit code, so '$37.00 / sleeve' resolves to OTHER with the supplier's own word kept as the label. The sheet records SLEEVE as free text.
  * BRAND IS NOT CAPTURED AS A FIELD. United Italian distribute 43 brands and print none of them in a column — only in the section banner, which is kept as evidence. The sheet leaves brand blank on all eighteen of its rows, so nothing corroborates what we would extract.
  * Every page is headed 'BONUS TERMS FOR BULK PURCHASE' but no tier or threshold is printed anywhere; the terms come from their sales desk. The only bulk fact on the page is the case price on the intravenous rows.
  * Where a merged cell carries both prices, the case price is not captured — the second price has no column of its own to be addressed by. The COST is unaffected.
  * The document costs 39 vision calls per ingestion, one per product page. Its text layer is excellent but deliberately unused: it linearises the multi-column tables into per-cell lines no contract could map.

expected_semantics.reason: Two prices on one row: $46.00 buys one bag, $828.00 the box of eighteen. The COST is the per-unit price — the golden sheet records exactly this, basis BAG at $46.00 — and the case price is kept beside it as a bulk term rather than thrown away. Taking the second would overstate the cost of a single bag eighteenfold. The basis is read from the price cell itself, not declared by the contract, because this supplier prints twenty-three different ones.

expected_semantics.reason: A hundred of something, in nothing named — 106 of the list's priced lines read this way. PACK rather than BOX on the 2026-09-01 ruling: the supplier stated the quantity and withheld the vessel, and naming one would be our invention. The golden sheet records BOX here, which is a container this page never prints; the price agrees to the cent. The Code names a RANGE of four sizes at one price, recorded as printed — whether it becomes one offering or four is the desk's decision.

source.text_excerpt: 89471 | Brachial Angiography Drape, 41” x 31” (Sterile) | (50’s / case) | $52.00 / pc

expected_semantics.reason: The row that shows why the basis must be read and never assumed. The page says fifty to a case AND that the price is per piece; the golden sheet says $52.00 buys the case. One of the two is wrong by a factor of fifty on the cost of every drape purchased. The contract reads what the supplier printed and the disagreement is pinned rather than quietly resolved — if BizOps correct the sheet the test says so, and if they confirm CASE then this page has been misread and the contract needs revisiting.
